gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in Allstate Protection Plans' robot drop test (reported by Notebookcheck), a bare iPhone 17 Pro and a bare iPhone Air both broke their front glass falling 6 ft face-down, while the 17 Pro dropped back-down got only cosmetic damage. For these phones, a case protects mainly through its raised screen lip or screen cover, not its back armor.
standout_why: I compared against Good Housekeeping (cited, 2026-02-05). Its Lab drop-tested the OtterBox Defender Pro but gives no height, count or surface, and it has no figures for the screen lip or for which side breaks. Travel + Leisure (cited) blocked me. I read its method through rottenwifi.com's write-up instead: 5 drops from 4 ft onto cement, turf and carpet, one 8 ft drop, and a throw down stairs. The 20 ft (UAG) and 13 ft (Speck) figures there are tied to T+L, but other figures on that page are makers' drop ratings. None of these pages, nor Macworld (no measured figures) or TechGearLab (none of the four candidates), says which face of an iPhone 17 breaks in a fall, or measures how far a candidate's lip stands above the screen.
decides: It supports giving weight to screen-side protection. The SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle Pro ($32.79 in ChatGPT's answer) covers the glass with a built-in screen protector. The other three rely on a raised lip, and the UAG Monarch Pro's lip was measured at about 1.5 mm above the screen. The page should tell Defender Pro, Monarch Pro and Tough Armor T buyers to add a glass screen protector. It does not overturn the OtterBox Defender Pro as the pick for the most drop protection, because no named reviewer published a like-for-like drop result that ranks the four cases.

findings.label: 6 ft face-down drop, no case (Allstate Protection Plans DropBot)
findings.value: Front Ceramic Shield 2 glass shattered at once from 6 ft face-down; phone kept working. Back-down drop: cosmetic damage only.
findings.source_title: iPhone Air and 17 Pro shatter in new drop test, despite strong bend resistance (Notebookcheck, Anubhav Sharma, 2025-09-23)
findings.note: Allstate Protection Plans ran the robotic DropBot test and Notebookcheck reported it. The article doesn't state the surface or the height of the back-down drop. Allstate's Jason Siciliano put the repair at up to $749 without AppleCare.

findings.label: 6 ft face-down drop, no case (Allstate Protection Plans DropBot)
findings.value: Front glass shattered at once from 6 ft face-down. Back-down drop cracked the rear panel. Phone kept working both times.
findings.source_title: iPhone Air and 17 Pro shatter in new drop test, despite strong bend resistance (Notebookcheck, 2025-09-23)
findings.note: Same Allstate test. Bend test: the Air bent at 190 lb and the 17 Pro at 200 lb, and both worked normally afterwards. Repair up to $699 without AppleCare.

findings.product: UAG Monarch Pro Kevlar (iPhone 17 Pro Max)
findings.label: Screen lip and camera lip measured by reviewer
findings.value: Rubber lip about 1.5 mm beyond the screen. 3 mm lip around the camera that stands a little more than 1 mm above the lenses. Buttons stand 1 mm out from the case.
findings.source_title: UAG Monarch Pro Kevlar iPhone 17 Pro Max Case review: think of it as insurance (The Gadgeteer, Pat Henderson, 2025-10-29)
findings.note: The reviewer's own lip figures; the measuring method isn't stated. The 2 oz (56.7 g) weight and the 25 ft / 5X MIL-SPEC 810G-516.6 rating on the same page are UAG specs quoted in the spec list, not measurements. The reviewer did not drop-test the case.

findings.product: Spigen Tough Armor T MagFit (iPhone 17 Pro)
findings.label: Case size and weight, plus bulk added to the phone (iDrop News)
findings.value: 6.15 × 3.07 × 0.59 in, 1.8 oz. iDrop News says the case makes the phone 'nearly a quarter-inch wider and about 25% heavier'.
findings.source_title: iPhone 17 Pro Case Review: Spigen's Tough Armor T vs. the Rugged Armor (iDrop News Staff, 2025-11-03)
findings.note: The article doesn't say whether the case was weighed or the figure came from Spigen. 1.8 oz ÷ 7.27 oz (the 206 g phone) ≈ 25%. For comparison, the Spigen Rugged Armor is 0.62 in deep and 1.4 oz. No drop test was done.

findings.label: Good Housekeeping Institute lab drop test
findings.value: In the GHI Lab drop tester the case left the test phone unscathed. GH says DROP+ certification means it was tested to survive multiple drops from at least 4 ft.
findings.source_title: I Tried 25 iPhone Cases—These Are the Ones That Survived Our Drop Tests (Good Housekeeping, Olivia Lipski, 2026-02-05)
findings.note: Read through the r.jina.ai reader because the site blocked a direct fetch. GH gives no height, count or surface for its own drops. This rival page is cited, so the finding is not new.
